thread:
jordan: Heads-up — proposing we tighten first-touch SLA for inbound leads to 5m. HubSpot -> Salesforce handoffs are where we lose momentum, especially when enrichment webhooks lag. Want to propose a fast-handoff path that preserves SDR velocity. Thoughts?

leah: 5m is aggressive. What's our current median? Any risk of flooding SDRs with low-quality leads if we bypass enrichment? :thinking_face:

nik: Quick data from last 30d: median HS->SF first-touch = 18m, mean = 32m. Inbound total = 3.2k, routed to SDR queue = 820, unclaimed within 15m = 210 (26%). Of those unclaimed, ~42% correlate with enrichment calls >3m.

amanda: We can implement a bypass for "first-touch" where we skip enrichment synchronously if lead_score >= 70 and route immediately. Enrichment runs async and updates records later. Lowers latency risk.

ryan: Logs confirm enrichment worker timeouts are set to 120s, but HubSpot webhook retries/backoff can extend end-to-end to 6-8m for some flows. Example trace snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:22Z] hs-webhook  -> received lead 3051
[2026-03-15T14:03:23Z] enrichment-worker  -> call third-party API (timeout 120s)
[2026-03-15T14:08:12Z] hs-retry  -> webhook retry #3 (backoff)
```

jordan: Proposed workflow patch for HubSpot workflows (pseudo): 
```yaml
- name: fast-handoff
  trigger: new_lead
  conditions:
    - lead_score >= 70
  actions:
    - route_to_sales_queue: SDR-primary
    - async: enqueue_enrichment_job
    - add_tag: fast-handoff
```

leah: If we do this, we need an SDR playbook: who owns the fallback if enrichment updates change routing info, and do we require SDRs to re-evaluate if enrichment downgrades the score? Also want metric list: first_touch_time, claim_rate_5m, enrichment_latency_90p.

opsbot: Deploy preview: hs-workflows/fast-handoff v1 -> staging (canary flag: 10%) :rocket:

jordan: Canary proposal: enable for 10% of inbound leads with score >= 70 for 48h. @amanda can you draft the SDR playbook and the re-eval steps? @nik can you add dashboards for claim_rate_5m and enrichment_latency_90p and hook alerts?

nik: On it. I'll add dashboards and alerts: 
- alert: claim_rate_5m < 70% -> notify #marketing + page #eng-oncall
- alert: enrichment_latency_90p > 2m -> notify #eng-infra
I'll also log fast-handoff tag to filter quality metrics.

amanda: I'll draft the playbook today. Quick note — we'll measure lead quality delta after bypass (conversion rate, rep feedback). If NPS/lead-quality drops >5% we'll roll back.

jordan: Timeline: canary by Mon, monitor 48h, full roll after 2 business days if no regressions. Doc draft link (WIP): https://redwood.company/internal/fast-handoff-playbook — add comments there. :thumbsup:

ryan: Small ops note — make sure the async enrichment worker idempotency handles updates after route to avoid duplication. Also suggest spike to increase enrichment worker concurrency if retries spike.

leah: Sounds good. Thanks all — excited to see if this improves SDR throughput.

jordan: Thanks — will post results and dashboard links once canary runs. :white_check_mark:
